## What is data?

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; height: 30vh; font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: bold;">

“All is data”

</div>

everything happening in  counts as data, including interviews, observations, documents, and background context.

<div style="font-size: 0.5em; text-align: center;">
Glaser, Barney G. "All Is Data." Grounded Theory Review, vol. 6, no. 2, 2007, pp. 1–22.
</div>

## What is data?

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;  font-size: 1.5em;">

"information, especially facts or numbers, collected to be examined and considered and used to help decision-making, or information in an electronic form that can be stored and used by a computer" 
</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.5em; text-align: center;">
Cambridge dictionary
</div>


## Data came in different type 

Some terminology

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}


![](CV_pictures/qualitative.jpg)
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}


- Profile statement → _Qualitative_
- Profile photo  → _Image_
:::

:::






## Data came in different type 

Some terminology

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}


![](CV_pictures/quantitative.jpg)
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}


**Quantitative**:  


- Age, salary, years of experience → _quantitative / continuous_
- Number of language spoken → _quantitative / discrete_

:::

:::






## Data came in different type 

Some terminology

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="40%"}


![](CV_pictures/categorical.png)
:::

::: {.column width="60%"}

- Location, nationality, driving licence → nominal
- Skill levels, language proficiency → ordinal
:::

:::
